data.name: Dinakaran
data.gender_notes: Dinakaran is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Dinakaran is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Dina' meaning 'day' and 'Kara' meaning 'doer' or 'giver'. This name is given to a child born during the daytime or to one who is believed to bring happiness and prosperity to others. The name Dinakaran carries the meaning “Day Giver” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dinakaran usually hope their child will grow to embody day giver and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Dinakaran belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Day Giver.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dinakaran total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: In Tamil Nadu, India, the name Dinakaran is considered to be auspicious as it signifies the child is born during the auspicious hours of the day. The child is believed to bring joy and prosperity not only to his or her own family but also to the community. It is also a common name among devotees of Lord Murugan (Subramanya) or Lord Vinayaka (Ganesh), as they believe that these deities are the givers (Karnan) of 'Dinam' or 'Dharma' or 'Dakshina' (charity, wealth, or offerings).
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dinakaran holds deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes the child being a giver, a donor, or a doer of good deeds (Karan) throughout the day (Dina). This name inspires one to lead a meaningful life by doing selfless acts and offering help and support to others, making the world a better place. As Lord Murugan and Lord Vinayaka are believed to grant the blessings of prosperity, wisdom, and victory over challenges, having the name Dinakaran is also considered to be an invocation to these deities for their blessings and guidance throughout life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dinakaran signifies one who carries the divine days ( Dinam = days, Karan = carrier). It symbolizes being in harmony with the cyclical rhythm of time and the cosmos.

historical_references.reference: Dinakaran was a prominent poet and scholar during the Alwar period of Tamil Nadu, around the 12th century CE. He was one of the 63 Nayanars, or saints, in Shaivism, a branch of Hinduism. Dinakaran's works are known for their devotional and poetic aspects, and he is particularly revered for his hymns in praise of Lord Shiva.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Dinakaran is found in the 17th century CE work 'Periyapuranam', a Tamil epic poem compiled by Sage Agastya. In this work, Dinakaran is described as a great sage who attained enlightenment through his devotion to Lord Shiva, and his soul merged into the divine being.
